# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("McNally_2011_mxylene_pbpk"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2011.00031>\n")
```

* Description: `r ui$description`

McNally, Cotton and Loizou (2011) propose a two-step global sensitivity
analysis (SA) workflow for PBPK models -- Morris screening followed by the
extended Fourier amplitude sensitivity test (eFAST), presented as a "Lowry
plot" -- and demonstrate it on a human PBPK model for inhaled m-xylene with
a bladder compartment for its urinary metabolite 3-methylhippuric acid (MHA).
The model is printed in full: parameter point values and SA ranges in
Table 1, the MHA equations in Methods, and the acslX CSL listing in the
Appendix. This article packages that model; the SA itself is a method applied
to the model and is illustrated only qualitatively below.

## Structure

* **Parent m-xylene.** Four flow-limited tissue compartments -- liver,
  adipose, rapidly perfused and slowly perfused tissue (Figure 1). Arterial
  blood is algebraic: the lung is at steady state, so
  `CA = (QC * CV + QP * CI) / (QC + QP / Pba)`, with `CI` the inhaled air
  concentration (ppm converted to mg/L through the ideal-gas molar volume
  24450 mL/mol) and `CV` the flow-weighted mixed venous return.
* **Metabolism.** Saturable Michaelis-Menten oxidation in the liver on the
  hepatic venous concentration. The in vivo Vmax is the in vitro microsomal
  rate (pmol/min/mg protein) scaled by the microsomal protein yield (MPY,
  mg/g liver) and the liver mass.
* **MHA.** Every mole of m-xylene metabolised becomes a mole of MHA in blood
  (`MRLi * MW_MHA / MW_xyl`), which moves first-order (`K1`) into the bladder.
  The bladder fills with urine at a constant rate `Rurine` and is emptied at
  each void; the urinary MHA concentration is expressed in mmol/mol
  creatinine through a fixed urinary creatinine concentration `CRE`.
* **Voiding** is not part of the ODE system: it is an event-table record
  (`evid = 5`, `amt = 0`) that resets the bladder MHA amount (`a_mha_bladder`)
  and urine volume (`urine_vol`) to zero, exactly as the CSL `DISCRETE
  urination` block does. `Curine` observed at a void time, just before the
  reset, is the concentration of the voided urine.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- ui$population
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Field = names(pop), Value = vapply(pop, function(x) paste(format(x), collapse = ", "), character(1))),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

The model is a single 75 kg reference adult (Table 1 point values). The
volunteer study used to illustrate it (groups of four volunteers exposed for
4 h on two occasions to a target 40 ppm m-xylene vapour in the Health and
Safety Laboratory controlled-atmosphere facility) is not reported further in
this paper. Figure 2 shows two of those volunteers.

# Simulation helper

The CSL listing voids at 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14 h after the start of exposure
(`urinationTime`); the same schedule is used here. A reset record sits a
numerical epsilon after each void so that the observation at the void time
reads the bladder before it is emptied.

```{r sim-helper}
mod <- ui
voids <- c(4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14)

make_events <- function(ids, tmax = 32, dt = 0.05, voids_h = voids, wt = 75) {
  grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, tmax, by = dt), voids_h)))
  obs <- expand.grid(time = grid, id = ids) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "a_liver", amt = NA_real_)
  resets <- expand.grid(
    time = voids_h + 1e-6, id = ids,
    cmt = c("a_mha_bladder", "urine_vol"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) |>
    mutate(evid = 5L, amt = 0)
  bind_rows(obs, resets) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid == 0L)) |>
    mutate(WT = wt) |>
    select(id, time, evid, cmt, amt, WT)
}

simulate <- function(params = NULL, ...) {
  ev <- make_events(ids = 1L, ...)
  out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, params = params, returnType = "data.frame"))
  if (is.null(out$id)) out$id <- 1L
  out
}

base <- simulate()
```

# Mass balance

Everything inhaled and not exhaled must be in a tissue or already
metabolised. This is a closed-form identity of the ODE system, so the bound
is tight.

```{r mass-balance}
last <- tail(base, 1)
absorbed <- last$a_inhaled - last$a_exhaled
in_body <- with(last, a_rapidly_perfused + a_slowly_perfused + a_fat + a_liver + a_metabolized)
mha_formed <- last$a_metabolized * 193.2 / 106.17
mha_accounted <- last$a_mha_blood + sum(base$a_mha_bladder[base$time %in% voids]) + last$a_mha_bladder
data.frame(
  quantity = c("m-xylene absorbed (mg)", "m-xylene in body + metabolised (mg)",
               "MHA formed (mg)", "MHA in blood + voided + bladder (mg)"),
  value = signif(c(absorbed, in_body, mha_formed, mha_accounted), 6)
) |> knitr::kable()
stopifnot(abs(absorbed / in_body - 1) < 1e-5)
stopifnot(abs(mha_accounted / mha_formed - 1) < 1e-4)
```

# Replicating Figure 2

Figure 2 overlays model predictions "using mean point values" on two
volunteers' venous blood m-xylene (panel A) and urinary MHA (panel B). The
model line and the observations below were digitised by the maintainers from
the published figure by eye (panel A to about 0.05 umol/L, panel B to about
5 mmol/mol creatinine).

```{r fig2-digitised}

```{r figure-2a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2A of McNally 2011: venous blood m-xylene during and after a 4-h, 40 ppm exposure. Line: packaged model; dashed line: published model line (digitised); points: published volunteer data (digitised)."}
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = base, aes(time, Cc_umol)) +
  geom_line(data = fig2a_line, aes(time, cv), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +

  theme_bw()
```

```{r figure-2b, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2B of McNally 2011: MHA in voided urine. Steps: packaged model, each void's concentration held until the next void as in the CSL listing; dashed: published model line (digitised); points: published volunteer data (digitised)."}
voided <- base |>
  filter(time %in% voids) |>
  select(void = time, Curine)
steps <- bind_rows(voided, tibble(void = 32, Curine = tail(voided$Curine, 1)))
ggplot() +
  geom_step(data = steps, aes(void, Curine)) +
  geom_step(
    data = bind_rows(fig2b_line, tibble(void = 32, curine = 12)),
    aes(void, curine), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40"
  ) +
  geom_point(data = fig2b_obs, aes(time, curine, shape = volunteer)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Curine (mmol/mol creatinine)", shape = "Volunteer") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figure-2-compare}
cmp_b <- voided |>
  inner_join(fig2b_line, by = "void") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Curine - curine) / curine)
cmp_a <- base |>
  filter(abs(time - round(time)) < 1e-9) |>
  select(time, Cc_umol) |>
  inner_join(fig2a_line, by = "time") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc_umol - cv) / cv)
cmp_b |>
  dplyr::rename("Void (h)" = void, "Model Curine" = Curine,
                "Published line" = curine, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
cmp_a |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "Model CV (umol/L)" = Cc_umol,
                "Published line" = cv, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

Urinary MHA (panel B) tracks the paper's own step line within about 20% at
every void, with the largest gap at the first void -- consistent with
reading the step heights off the figure by eye. Venous blood m-xylene
(panel A) peaks at 3.2 umol/L at the end of exposure against about 3.9 on the
published solid line, roughly 19% low, and the observed end-of-exposure
values (2.7 and 3.7 umol/L) bracket it. The published line also rises faster
in the first hour and decays more slowly after 10 h than the packaged model.
The maintainers re-coded the CSL listing's own 25-parameter variant (lung,
kidney and brain added, alveolar ventilation fixed at 350 L/h, the listing's
individual constants) as a check: it peaks at 3.2 umol/L at 4 h and falls to
0.03 umol/L by 23 h, the same as the packaged model. The published panel A
solid line therefore cannot be regenerated from the paper's own tables or
code, so no assertion ties the model to it; the packaged model is not tuned
to it (see Errata).

```{r figure-2-assert, echo = FALSE}
# Deterministic typical-value solve, so the bounds are on numerical agreement
# with a by-eye digitisation of the figure, not on sampling noise. The
# envelope is deliberately loose: the reference is the step height read off
# Figure 2B, not a reported number. No assertion ties the model to the
# unreproducible panel-A solid line (see Errata).
stopifnot(nrow(cmp_b) == 6L)
stopifnot(max(abs(cmp_b$pct_diff)) < 25)
# Monotone decline and a first void in the right band -- structural features
# that a mis-transcribed metabolism or bladder constant would break.
stopifnot(all(diff(voided$Curine) < 0))
stopifnot(voided$Curine[1] > 180, voided$Curine[1] < 270)
peak <- max(base$Cc_umol)
stopifnot(peak > 2.9, peak < 3.4)
stopifnot(abs(base$time[which.max(base$Cc_umol)] - 4) < 0.06)
# The two volunteers' end-of-exposure venous values bracket the model peak.
stopifnot(peak > 2.71, peak < 3.73)
```

# Exposure concentration (Figure 5 scenarios)

Figure 5 repeats the analysis at 40, 200 and 500 ppm. The dose dependence
comes from hepatic saturation: below KM the venous concentration scales
almost linearly with exposure, above it disproportionately.

```{r exposure-levels}
levels_ppm <- c(40, 200, 500)
by_level <- bind_rows(lapply(levels_ppm, function(ppm) {
  simulate(params = c(conc_air_ppm = ppm)) |> mutate(ppm = ppm)
}))
km_mgl <- 11.8 * 106.17 / 1000
summary_level <- by_level |>
  group_by(ppm) |>
  summarise(
    cv_peak_umol = max(Cc_umol),
    hepatic_venous_peak_over_km = max(Cliver / (279 / 19)) / km_mgl,
    metabolised_mg = max(a_metabolized),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(cv_peak_per_ppm = cv_peak_umol / ppm)
summary_level |>
  dplyr::rename("Exposure (ppm)" = ppm, "Peak CV (umol/L)" = cv_peak_umol,
                "Peak hepatic venous conc. / KM" = hepatic_venous_peak_over_km,
                "Metabolised by 32 h (mg)" = metabolised_mg,
                "Peak CV per ppm" = cv_peak_per_ppm) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(diff(summary_level$cv_peak_per_ppm) > 0))
```

```{r exposure-plot, fig.cap = "Venous blood m-xylene at the three exposure concentrations of Figure 5 (log scale)."}
ggplot(by_level, aes(time, Cc_umol, colour = factor(ppm))) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "CV (umol/L)", colour = "ppm") +
  theme_bw()
```
# Parameter ranking over the Table 1 ranges

The eFAST analysis in the paper took about 13 hours per output. As a cheap,
qualitative check that the packaged model responds to the parameters the
paper found important, each Table 1 parameter is moved one at a time to the
ends of its Table 1 range and the resulting change in two outputs is
recorded: the venous blood peak (the CV dose metric) and the first-void
urinary MHA (the Curine dose metric). One-at-a-time swings are not
variance-based indices, so this only checks that the influential parameters
are influential here too, not the exact ranking. The respiratory dead space
`DS` is not part of the model (see Errata).

```{r oat}
ranges <- tibble::tribble(
  ~parameter, ~name, ~low, ~high,
  "BW", "WT", 49, 92,
  "QCC", "qc_per_kg", 10, 20,
  "KM", "km_umol", 9.1, 14.6,
  "Vmax", "vmax_invitro", 761, 1028,
  "MPY", "mppgl", 18, 75,
  "QPC", "qp_per_kg", 10, 20,
  "Pba", "pc_blood_air", 12, 26,
  "Pfaa", "pc_fat_air", 1400, 2200,
  "Plia", "pc_liver_air", 150, 350,
  "QspdC", "fq_slowly_perfused", 0.2, 0.35,
  "VfaC", "fv_fat", 0.07, 0.28,
  "VliC", "fv_liver", 0.02, 0.031,
  "Rurine", "urprod", 0.06, 0.115,
  "CRE", "c_creat_urine", 7, 15,
  "K1", "kurine_mha", 2, 18
)

metrics <- function(params) {
  s <- simulate(params = params)
  c(cv_peak = max(s$Cc_umol),
    curine_first = s$Curine[s$time == voids[1]][1])
}
baseline <- metrics(NULL)

oat <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ranges)), function(i) {
  lo <- metrics(setNames(ranges$low[i], ranges$name[i]))
  hi <- metrics(setNames(ranges$high[i], ranges$name[i]))
  tibble(
    parameter = ranges$parameter[i],
    cv_peak_swing_pct = 100 * (hi["cv_peak"] - lo["cv_peak"]) / baseline["cv_peak"],
    curine_swing_pct = 100 * (hi["curine_first"] - lo["curine_first"]) / baseline["curine_first"]
  )
}))

oat |>
  arrange(desc(abs(cv_peak_swing_pct))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Parameter" = parameter,
                "CV peak swing (%)" = cv_peak_swing_pct,
                "Curine swing (%)" = curine_swing_pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The parameters that move the venous blood peak most -- the blood:air
partition coefficient `Pba`, ventilation `QPC`, cardiac output `QCC` and the
metabolic parameters `KM` / `Vmax` / `MPY` -- are the ones the paper's Morris
and eFAST analyses rank at the top for CV (Table 2, Figure 4A,B). The urinary
MHA metric is dominated by the urine-production rate `Rurine` and urinary
creatinine `CRE`, exactly as the paper reports for Curine (Figure 4C,D). The
ordering within those groups differs because a one-at-a-time swing is not an
eFAST index, but the influential set matches.

```{r oat-assert, echo = FALSE}
top_cv <- oat |> arrange(desc(abs(cv_peak_swing_pct))) |> head(6) |> dplyr::pull(parameter)
stopifnot(all(c("Pba", "QPC") %in% top_cv))
top_cu <- oat |> arrange(desc(abs(curine_swing_pct))) |> head(3) |> dplyr::pull(parameter)
stopifnot(all(c("Rurine", "CRE") %in% top_cu))
```

# NCA characterisation of the venous blood profile

The paper reports a sensitivity analysis, not a non-compartmental PK table,
so there are no published Cmax / AUC values to compare against. PKNCA is used
here to characterise the simulated venous blood m-xylene profile and to lock
the shape (a sharp end-of-exposure peak followed by multi-phase decay) against
regression. A time-zero record is added defensively so the AUC starts at the
first measurement.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- base |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = "40 ppm, 4 h") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
if (!any(nca_conc$time == 0)) {
  nca_conc <- bind_rows(
    transmute(filter(nca_conc, time == min(time)), id, time = 0, Cc = 0, treatment),
    nca_conc
  )
}

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | id / treatment)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = max(nca_conc$time),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(res)

nca_tab |>
  select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  mutate(PPORRES = signif(PPORRES, 4)) |>
  dplyr::rename("NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD, "Value (mg/L units)" = PPORRES) |>
  knitr::kable()

cmax <- nca_tab$PPORRES[nca_tab$PPTESTCD == "cmax"]
tmax <- nca_tab$PPORRES[nca_tab$PPTESTCD == "tmax"]
stopifnot(abs(tmax - 4) < 0.06)
stopifnot(abs(cmax - max(base$Cc)) < 1e-6)
```

The NCA peak falls at 4 h -- the end of the exposure window -- as expected for
an inhalation profile with no post-exposure input, and the half-life reflects
the slow terminal release from adipose tissue (fat:blood partition
coefficient about 100).

# Assumptions and deviations / Errata

* **Respiratory dead space `DS` (Table 1, 0.3) is not in the model.** The CSL
  listing computes `QPa = QP * (1 - DS)` but the gas-exchange equation uses
  the undiminished ventilation `QPMC` (fixed at 350 L/h in the listing), and
  the alveolar-ventilation term never enters the arterial equation reduced by
  `DS`. The paper's own sensitivity results confirm `DS` is inert: its
  main-effect index is 9.18e-07 (Appendix Lowry-plot data) and it ranks last
  for both outputs (Table 2). The packaged model therefore applies ventilation
  without the dead-space reduction, matching the listing's behaviour.

* **KM units.** Table 1 prints the Michaelis constant as "11.8 mMol L-1",
  but the CSL listing carries it as `Km2E1 = 1.253` mg/L, which is
  11.8 umol/L x 106.17 g/mol / 1000. The value is therefore micromolar, not
  millimolar; the Table 1 unit label is a typo. The model stores
  `km_umol = 11.8` umol/L and converts to mg/L internally, reproducing the
  listing's 1.253 mg/L.

* **Table 1 point values vs the CSL listing.** The packaged model uses the
  Table 1 point values throughout (BW 75 kg, Pba 19, four tissues). The
  Appendix CSL listing is a later 25-parameter variant with lung, kidney and
  brain added, a different body mass (79 kg), blood:air PC (15.1), adipose
  and slowly-perfused fractions, and alveolar ventilation fixed at 350 L/h.
  Both forms give the same venous peak (about 3.2 umol/L at 4 h) and the same
  terminal level; the four-tissue Table 1 form is packaged because Table 1 is
  the parameter set the paper tabulates with its SA ranges.

* **Figure 2A published line.** The solid model line in Figure 2A peaks near
  3.9 umol/L and decays more slowly than either the packaged model or the
  CSL listing's own 25-parameter variant reproduces (both about 3.2 umol/L
  and faster terminal decay). The published line cannot be regenerated from
  the paper's tables or its Appendix code. The packaged model is deliberately
  **not** tuned to it; its venous peak is bracketed by the two volunteers'
  observed end-of-exposure values (2.7 and 3.7 umol/L).

* **No IIV, no residual error.** This is a deterministic typical-value PBPK
  model evaluated with mean point values, as in the paper. The sensitivity
  analysis treats the Table 1 ranges as uniform input distributions for a
  variance decomposition; those ranges are recorded in `covariateData`
  (for body weight) and in the source trace above, not as random effects.

* **K1 provenance.** The blood-to-urine rate constant K1 = 10 /h is a Table 1
  value the authors estimated externally (from digitised Engstrom et al. 1978
  post-exposure urinary-excretion data), then used as a fixed constant here.
